text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: CRITICAL - host-gpu-23 triggered watchdog timeout (kernel_watchdog). Pager: PD#INC-88512. Auto-page at 3961234567. Node heartbeats lost, kubelet NotReady.

jane: acked. I'm on it.

alex: I'm looking — `kubectl get nodes host-gpu-23 -o wide` shows NotReady, lastTransitionTime a few seconds ago. Pod count still present.

maria: any customer-facing impact yet? any requests failing?

jane: quick checks, a couple of inference requests are timing out hitting that rack. Router fallback kicked in but SLA latencies spiked ~2xx ms for a handful of tenants. Not full outage.

alex: grabbing serial console now. Using `ssh console-hosting host-gpu-23` then `sudo dmidecode` to confirm hardware.

sre-lead: good. if kernel watchdog, treat as host-level crash. We should cordon and drain to reduce blast radius. Plan: cordon -> drain -> evacuate pods -> RMA if hardware.

jane: running: `kubectl cordon host-gpu-23`

jane: `kubectl drain host-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` in progress. Not all pods are evacuating cleanly (some long-running pinned workloads).

alex: serial console output shows repeating: `kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 24s` then `kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog` — looks like a kernel watchdog loop. Pasting recent lines:
```
[  123.456789] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 24s
[  124.123456] kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog
[  124.123500] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/3 Not tainted 5.10.0-redwood #42
```

maria: flagged PD incident ticket for customer ops, added note that traffic fallback occurred, minor latency spikes for ~3 tenants. No request loss recorded so far.

incidentbot: PagerDuty update: incident PD#INC-88512 acknowledged by jane at 3961234590. Escalation path intact.

ops-bot: autoscaler/placement note: transient capacity drop may cause short scheduling delays for queued jobs. Suggest increasing dedicated burst pool by 1 slot if available. Command: `infractl capacity bump --pool=gpu-burst --count=1`

sre-lead: Alex, can you confirm if this is reproducible across other hosts in same rack? Could be PSU or BMC flakiness.

alex: checking dmesg and BMC logs. BMC reachable but reports a host reset at ~3961234558. IPMI shows no thermal trip. Could be kernel bug triggered by driver update.

jane: drain completed for most pods; 4 pods failed to terminate due to FUSE mounts, I'm force-deleting them now with `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force`.

maria: I'm preparing a short customer notification: "We observed degraded latency affecting a small subset of inference requests in region us-west-2 around <time>. Traffic was routed to fallback capacity and there's no indication of lost data. We're investigating host-level failure on hardware host-gpu-23 and will update." Shall I send?

sre-lead: send now, mark as "under investigation". Add mitigation steps: drained host, traffic routed, investigating hardware+kernel logs.

hw-oncall: received hardware page. We'll check NVMe and power rails, but if kernel panic is consistent we'll schedule RMA. ETA to confirm 20m.

alex: rebooted the host from BMC to collect fresh logs on next boot. Boot fails into kernel panic prior to mounting root, so we captured serial logs to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/3961234567/serial.log

incidentbot: PagerDuty note added: event assigned to hardware oncall hw-oncall.

jane: handing off active mitigation to alex for the next 30m (he's on serial/BMC). I'll stay as incident comms and continue draining followups.

sre-lead: acknowledged handoff. I'll own the post-incident template and follow-up tasks (blameless postmortem, kernel version audit, model rollback checklist).

maria: sent customer note. Also flagged running eval jobs that relied on that node; they may need rescheduling.

ops-bot: `infractl placement fix` queued — will rebalance pods across healthy GPU hosts.

alex: update: BMC logs show a kernel oops at 3961234559 preceded by `nvidia: GPU reset completed` messages, then watchdog. Might be a driver/firmware interaction. Collected logs: /var/log/hosts/host-gpu-23/boot-logs-3961234567.tar.gz uploaded.

hw-oncall: confirmed power cycle and NVMe health checks passed. We're moving to RMA hold since kernel panics persisted after cleanboot with previous kernel. Opening hardware ticket HT#4821.

sre-lead: next steps and responsibilities:
- alex: preserve logs, coordinate RMA, confirm reintroduction steps
- jane: update timeline and customer comms if anything changes
- maria: inventory impacted tenants and follow up with account owners
- hw-oncall: RMA and hardware follow-through

jane: adding playbook ticket: OPS-1241 "host-gpu kernel-watchdog panic - postmortem & mitigations".

incidentbot: PagerDuty: incident PD#INC-88512 status: acknowledged -> in-progress. Last update 3961234599.

alex: handing back to oncall rotation in 45m. For now node is quarantined and drained. Will not reintroduce until kernel/driver root cause identified.

maria: closing customer note loop for now. Will reopen if partner reports errors.

sre-lead: thanks team. We'll collect artifacts and schedule a short async postmortem. If anyone finds model-specific bug trigger, ping research/eng-ml.

jane: signoff from me for the immediate paging response. Leaving log pointers and a brief timeline in the ticket. :thumbsup:
